points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 珍·古道尔1934年4月3日出生于英国伦敦。童年时期，她对动物表现出浓厚兴趣，尤其是对非洲的向往。她没有接受过正规大学教育，但在伦敦的秘书学校学习后，曾担任秘书工作。这段时期，她阅读了大量关于动物行为学的书籍，尤其是对黑猩猩的研究产生了浓厚兴趣。她曾前往肯尼亚，希望能研究野生动物，这一决定改变了她的人生轨迹。
points.descriptionEn: Born on April 3, 1934, in London, England, Jane Goodall showed an early fascination with animals, particularly with Africa. Without formal university education, she attended secretarial school and worked as a secretary. During this time, she extensively read about animal behavior, developing a special interest in chimpanzee research. Her decision to travel to Kenya to study wildlife marked a turning point in her life's trajectory.

points.title: 开创性研究
points.description: 1957年，古道尔在肯尼亚结识了著名古人类学家路易斯·利基，后者邀请她前往坦桑尼亚贡贝溪国家公园研究黑猩猩。1960年，她开始这项研究，最初面临黑猩猩的恐惧和不信任。通过耐心观察和命名个体黑猩猩，她逐渐获得了它们的信任。在此期间，她做出了多项重大发现：黑猩猩会使用工具（用树枝钓白蚁）、有复杂的社会结构、会制作工具、甚至有战争行为。这些发现彻底改变了人们对动物行为和人类进化的理解。
points.descriptionEn: In 1957, Goodall met renowned anthropologist Louis Leakey in Kenya, who invited her to study chimpanzees at Gombe Stream National Park in Tanzania. Beginning her research in 1960, she initially faced chimpanzees' fear and distrust. Through patient observation and naming individual chimps, she gradually gained their trust. During this period, she made several groundbreaking discoveries: chimpanzees using tools (fishing for termites with sticks), complex social structures, tool-making, and even warfare. These findings revolutionized understanding of animal behavior and human evolution.

points.title: 学术深造
points.description: 1965年，在路易斯·利基的安排下，古道尔进入剑桥大学攻读动物学博士学位，成为剑桥大学达尔文学院首位获得博士学位的学生。她的博士论文基于贡贝溪的研究成果，进一步巩固了她在学术界的地位。此后，她继续在剑桥进行学术研究，同时将贡贝溪的研究扩展到更长期的项目。这一时期，她出版了多部著作，包括《贡贝的黑猩猩》系列，向世界介绍她的研究成果。她的研究方法强调长期观察和个体识别，开创了动物行为学研究的新范式。
points.descriptionEn: In 1965, arranged by Louis Leakey, Goodall entered Cambridge University to pursue a PhD in animal behavior, becoming the first student at Darwin College to earn a doctorate. Her dissertation, based on Gombe research, solidified her academic standing. She continued her academic work at Cambridge while extending the Gombe project into a long-term study. During this period, she authored several books, including the 'Chimpanzees of Gombe' series, introducing her findings to the world. Her research methodology emphasized long-term observation and individual identification, creating a new paradigm in animal behavior studies.

points.title: 环保倡导
points.description: 1986年，古道尔离开了贡贝溪的研究现场，开始全职投身于环保事业。她成立了珍·古道尔研究会（Jane Goodall Institute），致力于保护黑猩猩及其栖息地，并推动全球环保教育。她走遍全球150多个国家，发表演讲，提高公众对野生动物保护的认识。她特别关注黑猩猩的非法贸易和栖息地破坏问题，推动建立保护区和野生动物救援中心。这一时期，她获得了多项国际荣誉，包括联合国和平使者称号，并成为联合国教科文组织的和平使者。她的工作从科学研究转向了更广泛的环保倡导。
points.descriptionEn: In 1986, Goodall left her field research at Gombe to dedicate herself full-time to environmental conservation. She founded the Jane Goodall Institute, focused on protecting chimpanzees and their habitats, and promoting global environmental education. She traveled to over 150 countries, giving lectures to raise public awareness about wildlife protection. She particularly addressed illegal chimpanzee trade and habitat destruction, establishing reserves and wildlife rescue centers. During this period, she received numerous international honors, including the UN Messenger of Peace designation, and became a UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador. Her work shifted from scientific research to broader environmental advocacy.

points.title: 遗产传承
points.description: 进入21世纪，古道尔继续她的环保工作，并特别关注青年环保教育。她创立了'根与芽'（Roots & Shoots）项目，鼓励全球青年参与环保行动。尽管年事已高，她仍保持每年300天以上的旅行和演讲日程，致力于环保教育。2010年，她获得了英国女爵爵位，成为英国历史上少数获得此荣誉的女性科学家。她的研究方法和发现至今影响着动物行为学、人类学和环保领域。她的一生从科学研究者转变为环保活动家，再到环保教育家，展现了科学家社会责任感的典范。
points.descriptionEn: Entering the 21st century, Goodall continued her environmental work with special focus on youth environmental education. She founded the 'Roots & Shoots' program, encouraging global youth to participate in conservation actions. Despite her age, she maintains a travel and speaking schedule of over 300 days annually, dedicated to environmental education. In 2010, she was made a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire, one of few female scientists to receive this honor. Her research methods and findings continue to influence animal behavior, anthropology, and conservation fields. Her evolution from scientist to activist to environmental educator exemplifies the social responsibility of scientists.

supporter.zh: 珍·古道尔被誉为动物行为学的先驱和环保运动的标志性人物。她的长期观察研究彻底改变了人类对动物行为的理解，证明了动物具有复杂情感和智慧。她开创的个体化研究方法为动物行为学树立了新标准。作为环保活动家，她通过珍·古道尔研究会和'根与芽'项目培养了新一代环保意识，她的工作激励了全球数百万人关注野生动物保护和环境保护。她的一生展现了科学家的社会责任感，证明了科学不仅可以解释世界，还可以改变世界。
supporter.en: Jane Goodall is hailed as a pioneer in animal behaviorology and an iconic figure in the environmental movement. Her long-term observational research revolutionized human understanding of animal behavior, demonstrating that animals possess complex emotions and intelligence. The individualized research methods she pioneered set new standards in animal behaviorology. As an environmental activist, she has cultivated a new generation of environmental awareness through the Jane Goodall Institute and Roots & Shoots program, inspiring millions worldwide to wildlife conservation and environmental protection. Her life exemplifies the social responsibility of scientists, proving that science can not only explain the world but also change it.

critic.zh: 批评者指出古道尔的研究方法存在科学严谨性不足的问题，她与黑猩猩建立了过于亲密的关系，可能影响了研究的客观性。一些科学家认为她的人类学倾向过于明显，将人类特征过度投射到动物行为上。此外，她的环保立场有时被视为过于理想化，忽视了发展中国家经济发展与环境保护之间的复杂平衡。批评者还指出，她将个人形象过度商业化，可能削弱了科学研究的严肃性。这些争议反映了科学研究中主观性与客观性、情感与理性之间的永恒张力。
critic.en: Critics point out that Goodall's research methods lacked scientific rigor, as she formed overly intimate relationships with chimpanzees, potentially compromising objectivity. Some scientists argue her anthropological tendencies were too pronounced, excessively projecting human characteristics onto animal behavior. Additionally, her environmental positions are sometimes seen as overly idealistic, neglecting the complex balance between economic development in developing countries and environmental protection. Critics also note her personal image became overly commercialized, potentially undermining the seriousness of scientific research. These controversies reflect the eternal tension between subjectivity and objectivity, emotion and reason in scientific research.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，珍·古道尔被定义为连接科学、环保与公众教育的桥梁式人物。她的贡贝溪研究被视为20世纪最重要的动物行为学研究之一，开创了长期野外观察的先河。在流行文化中，她已成为环保主义的象征，代表着人类与自然和谐共存的理想。她的研究方法虽然引发争议，但不可否认地推动了动物行为学的发展。从科学到环保再到教育，她的职业生涯展现了现代科学家角色的演变。她不仅改变了我们对黑猩猩的认识，也改变了我们对自己作为人类在自然界中位置的理解。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Jane Goodall is defined as a bridging figure connecting science, environmentalism, and public education. Her Gombe research is considered one of the most important studies in animal behaviorology of the 20th century, pioneering long-term field observation. In popular culture, she has become a symbol of environmentalism, representing the ideal of harmonious coexistence between humans and nature. While her research methods have been controversial, they undeniably advanced animal behaviorology. Her career from science to environmentalism to education reflects the evolution of the modern scientist's role. She not only changed our understanding of chimpanzees but also our perception of humanity's place in the natural world.

self.zh: 你不能通过了解一个人来了解全人类，但你可以通过了解一只黑猩猩来了解黑猩猩。
self.en: You can't get to know a human being by studying one human, but you can get to know a chimpanzee by studying one chimpanzee.

others.zh: 珍·古道尔的工作改变了我们看待动物的方式，也改变了我们看待自己的方式。她向我们展示了，科学不仅是关于事实的，也是关于关怀和责任的。
others.en: Jane Goodall's work has changed the way we look at animals and the way we look at ourselves. She has shown us that science is not just about facts, but also about compassion and responsibility.
